## Types

### FormatDescriptor

Static description of a format as the tool understands it.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | Short id used on the command line, e.g. `czi`. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | Human name, e.g. `Zeiss CZI`. |
| `vendor` | `string` | yes | Vendor (nominative use only). |
| `extensions` | array of `string` | yes | File extensions, lowercase, without the dot. |
| `family` | `string` | yes | Family: `microscopy`, `mass-spectrometry`, `flow-cytometry`, ... |
| `can_read` | `boolean` | yes | True when the tool can read this format. |
| `can_write` | `boolean` | yes | True when `export` can also write this format (e.g. mzML, OME-Zarr). |
| `confidence` | [`Confidence`](#confidence) | yes | Overall confidence in this reader. |
| `known_gaps` | array of `string` | yes | Things this reader knowingly does not handle yet. |

### Confidence

Per-format confidence summary shown by `info` and `self formats`.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"high"` | Validated against an oracle across the corpus; structure from vendor docs or a spec. |
| `"medium"` | Validated on the corpus; some fields inferred. |
| `"low"` | Early support; expect gaps. |
